findings.summary: One reason the plan gives for rejecting a run-time read is that readers cannot see docs/ontology.toml, yet the new error tells the reader to cite that file.
findings.evidence: Decision 1 says "The file is not in the plain copy readers see". System facts say readers get a plain copy of the files, without git or records/ only, so docs/ontology.toml should be in that copy. Step 4's error says "say which of its recorded senses applies and cite docs/ontology.toml". The two statements cannot both hold. Fix: Drop the plain-copy reason from the rejected alternative. The reasons about constant refusals and prompt scope are enough. Or check the claim and fix the error text to match.
findings.location: Plan decision 1 (rejected alternative: run-time read of docs/ontology.toml) vs. decision 3 and step 4 (error text)

findings.summary: The gated name comes from this repository's ontology but is compiled into a gate that sees every request. A request about some other 'Hermes' would be told to cite a file that may not describe it.
findings.evidence: check_defined_terms(reading, request) takes no repository input. refusing_check gets repo_files (reading.rs:657-668), but the new rule ignores it. The error tells the reader to cite docs/ontology.toml in every case. Fix: State in D165 and the doc comment that the list is Athena's own vocabulary and that the gate applies whatever the target. Or word the error "cite docs/ontology.toml when the repository has it". The signature does not need to change.
findings.location: Step 4, AMBIGUOUS_NAMES and the error text

findings.summary: The rewritten error drops the existing advice to cite the file that defines a structural term, which the doc comment still describes.
findings.evidence: The current error (reading.rs:3954) says "and cite the file that defines it if there is one", and the doc (reading.rs:3923) says "the line may cite the file that defines it". The planned text gives the citation advice only for ambiguous names. Fix: Keep "cite the file that defines it if there is one" for all terms, and add the sense-and-ontology clause for ambiguous names only.
findings.location: Step 4, the new generic error text

findings.summary: The accepted example names one sense. That is right for the 0wtc request, but it shows the one-sense limit the plan documents.
findings.evidence: The ontology says Hermes has two senses (docs/ontology.toml:86-89), and the 0wtc misread was a conflation of the two. Fix: Optionally make the fixture name the sense explicitly, for example "Term Hermes: Hermes Agent, the studied agent (sense 1 in docs/ontology.toml), not the Orchestration god". It would then model the repair the error asks for.
findings.location: Step 2, accepted fixture `Term Hermes: the studied self-improving agent, not part of Athena`

summary: The plan matches the accepted reading, and each criterion has a real seam and a demonstration that fails without the change. I checked the snapshot. check_defined_terms, structural_term, defined_terms and plain_request_prose are in reading.rs at lines 3864 to 3959, and STRUCTURAL_TERMS is at line 3724. mirrors::parse_ontology is pub at mirrors.rs:880, and OntologyTerm.name is at line 668. docs/ontology.toml holds exactly the seven names the plan partitions. D164 is the last decision, so D165 is the right next id. The recorded 0wtc request in CITED_REQUESTS (refusal_corpus.rs:483-487) has "Hermes Agent" in plain prose, outside quotes and outside any parenthesised example list. It returns None today, so the edited replay assertions really fail before the change. The existing needle tests hold: "covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs", "are not caught" and the 3% text that the D164 test reads by splitting on "## D164 ·" all stay true. The only other files that contain Hermes are mirrors and ontology fixtures, and none of them goes through the reading gate. The two-list partition test turns the one-element list into a mechanism, so a new ontology term fails the build until someone classifies it. That answers the round-1 concern that a hard-coded single name is a special case. Three minor issues remain. The reason given for rejecting a run-time read contradicts the new error text. The gate is compiled from this repository's vocabulary but applies to every request the gate sees. The new generic error drops the existing advice to cite a defining file for structural terms.
